data.title: Basic principles of the Hradiská civic association
data.excerpt: The Hradiská civic association is above all a community of volunteers interested in history, archaeology and the protection of cultural heritage. Metal detecting as such is not our priority: what matters is systematic, responsible and expert work for the benefit of knowledge about historical sites and their protection.
data.metaTitle: Basic principles of the Hradiská civic association
data.metaDescription: OZ Hradiská is a community of volunteers — its priority is not metal detecting but responsible, expert work for knowledge about heritage and its protection.

children.text: The Hradiská civic association (hereinafter the “association”) is above all a community of volunteers with an interest in history, archaeology and the protection of cultural heritage. Our priority is not metal detecting as such, but systematic, responsible and expert work for the benefit of knowledge about historical sites and their protection.

blocks.alt: Basic principles of the Hradiská civic association

children.text: 1. The mission and aims of the association

1. In accordance with the Statutes of the association, the basic aim of the association is to collect knowledge and information about hillforts in Slovakia, to publish it, thereby helping to keep the public informed, to develop tourism to hillfort sites and also to guide it, and at the same time to bring to those interested, in an engaging form, the immensely rich period of our national history – the Early Middle Ages, especially the times of Great Moravia. A further aim of the association is to learn about the earliest history of Slovakia, with a focus on the hillforts of the Slavs, the Celts and the earlier cultures which inhabited the territory of Slovakia in the past. The association therefore gives financial support to the authors of popular educational articles about hillforts in Slovakia.

2. In accordance with its basic aim, the association focuses on the rediscovery of old hillforts in Slovakia in the eyes of the public. For this purpose the association cooperates with the web portal www.hradiska.sk. Within its financial means, the association further arranges for the production of information panels about individual hillforts in Slovakia and for their installation in the field where such information is lacking.

3. The association also provides financial and media support for artistic work (pictorial, audiovisual and other works) whose subject is the hillforts of Slovakia and the history of the Slavs and the Celts in the territory of present-day Slovakia.
4. A further aim is to bring together individuals with an interest in the earliest history of Slovakia and to stimulate their creative activity in the fields outlined in point 3.

5. Not least, it is also an aim to cooperate with cultural and possibly other authorities and organisations and with civic associations in the field of the history and the beliefs of the Slavs and the Celts.
6. The OZH also cooperates with the professional and the lay public in fulfilling the aims of the civic association.

7. The activities of the association also include participation in official archaeological excavations with the use of metal detectors. Metal detecting is only one of the possible forms of cooperation and always takes place exclusively within the framework of the statutory rules, the methodology and specific permits.
2. Cooperation with archaeologists
Cooperation in the field of fieldwork takes place exclusively:
under the direction of authorised archaeologists,
on the basis of proper permits,
according to a strictly established methodology.
3. Prohibition of metal detecting without the consent and knowledge of an archaeologist

I. The Hradiská civic association is not a platform for providing cover for individual searching, nor for legalising private activities in the field without a permit (hereinafter searching “on one's own”).

II. A member of the association acknowledges that searching for archaeological finds without the permit of the competent monuments board is an illegal activity, and that in doing so he may commit an administrative offence in the field of the protection of archaeological heritage, or the criminal offence of damaging and devaluing archaeological heritage under § 249 of the Criminal Code.
III. A member of the association undertakes not to search with a metal detector on his own, without the knowledge of the archaeologists and the other members of the association.
IV. Should a member breach the above rule, he will be expelled from the association for it.

V. The association assumes no protection and no guarantee for anyone who searches with a metal detector without the permit of an archaeologist or of the competent monuments board. Membership of the association is in no case a mitigating circumstance in the event of a breach of this rule, or in the event of a breach of the law. Quite the contrary: in such a case the association will give the law-enforcement authorities full cooperation in the investigation of the former member of the association.
4. Conditions of membership
Membership of the association is not a formality. It requires:
a serious interest in history and in the protection of monuments,
a willingness to take part in varied volunteer work, not only in metal detecting,
respect for the statutory and ethical rules,
demonstrable and long-term cooperation with the association.
If an applicant is primarily a metal detectorist, the basic condition of further cooperation is:
settling the matter of all illegally found archaeological objects by duly handing them over to authorised archaeologists,
a commitment not to carry out individual searching on his own.
5. Confidentiality

Information about sites and excavations which we learn of in the association is considered confidential unless the members of the group agree (usually after consulting the archaeologists) that the information may be made public. Members will therefore not publish information about excavations in progress, especially on social networks. The same rule applies that finds from excavations which are accessible to members of the association may not be published anywhere publicly or passed outside the association without the permission of the archaeologists and without prior agreement with them.
6. Capacity

At present the association has no spare capacity for the systematic training of new members and for vouching for their activity. Cooperation is possible above all through gradual involvement in specific activities and excavations, where we can get to know one another in person and assess the possibilities of further involvement.
7. Alternatives for those interested in metal detecting

If someone is interested exclusively in metal detecting, we recommend turning directly to the competent regional monuments board and enquiring about the possibilities of legal volunteering within official projects. Our ambition is to build a community of people who understand the value of archaeological heritage, approach it with respect and are ready to invest their time and energy in meaningful volunteer work – not only in searching for finds, but in their protection, study and presentation to the public.
8. Metal detecting with us without membership of OZ Hradiská

If you are interested exclusively in metal detecting with us at archaeological excavations but are not a member of OZ Hradiská, you can get in touch at the e-mail address hradiska333@gmail.com as someone interested in helping at excavations. In that case we will, in some instances (after prior agreement with the archaeologist), inform you of the date and the site of the excavation being carried out and give you the contact details of the organiser. For helpers who are not members of the association, the association assumes no responsibility.
